responsibilities: ทำงานร่วมกับผู้ใช้งานหรือทีมพัฒนาธุรกิจ เพื่อรวบรวมและทำความเข้าใจความต้องการของระบบ
ออกแบบ พัฒนา และปรับแต่งคำสั่ง prompt เพื่อเพิ่มประสิทธิภาพการทำงานของ AI
ออกแบบโครงสร้างระบบ กระบวนการทำงาน และการใช้งานของ AI application
ใช้ Large Language Models (LLMs) เพื่อพัฒนา AI application
ทดสอบการทำงานและประเมินประสิทธิภาพของ AI application
ทำงานร่วมกับทีมวิศวกรซอฟต์แวร์อย่างใกล้ชิด เพื่อนำ AI application ไปใช้ในระบบจริง
qualifications: ชำนาญในการเขียนโปรแกรมด้วย Python, prompt engineering, และ context engineering
มีทักษะในการคิดวิเคราะห์และแก้ไขปัญหาได้อย่างดีเยี่ยม
มีความสนใจในด้าน AI ระบบอัตโนมัติ (automation) และ data-driven solutions
มีความเข้าใจพื้นฐานเกี่ยวกับ Natural Language Processing (NLP) และแนวคิดของ machine learning
มีประสบการณ์ในการทำงานกับ API, JSON หรือ automation pipelines
หากมีประสบการณ์การใช้งานเครื่องมือหรือเทคโนโลยี เช่น n8n, SQL, Docker หรือแพลตฟอร์ม Cloud จะได้รับการพิจารณาเป็นพิเศษ

scoring_semantics.meaning: Evidence-based alignment of a resume with this job definition.
does_not_represent: an automated hire or reject decision

education_analysis.missing_data_policy: Absent education metadata is not provided, is not inferred, and does not create a scoring penalty.

rating_scale.description: Mention only. The skill/tool/concept appears in a skills list or isolated statement with no demonstrated practical usage.
Limited practical evidence. The resume shows relevant usage or participation, but implementation depth, ownership, or demonstrated competency is limited or unclear.
Clear hands-on evidence. The resume explicitly shows practical implementation or substantial responsibility for the criterion in a project/work context.

Strong demonstrated evidence. The resume shows clear hands-on implementation PLUS criterion-relevant evidence of substantial depth, complexity, evaluation, or outcome. Do not assign Level 4 merely because the evidence contains numbers, percentages, latency, cost, sample counts, or other metrics; the measurable result must materially demonstrate strength in the criterion being scored.

match_types.definition: Resume evidence explicitly demonstrates the requested competency or an unmistakable implementation of it. Direct must not depend on speculative assumptions about unseen implementation details.

Evidence demonstrates substantially the same underlying competency using a different but genuinely equivalent terminology/implementation. Equivalence must be defensible from the resume evidence itself. Do not use 'equivalent' merely because two concepts belong to the same broad technical domain.

Resume evidence explicitly demonstrates functionally similar and meaningfully transferable experience, but is not the requested technology or capability itself, such as Make.com for n8n. Do not infer transferable experience from unrelated or unsupported claims.
Evidence demonstrates a related capability, but not the requested competency itself. Requires an inference from a neighboring activity. Adjacent evidence must not be described as direct.
No resume evidence supports the criterion. Related technology/domain alone is insufficient.

missing_information_principles: missing information is not negative evidence
absence of evidence is not evidence of absence

non_scoring_signals.ai_automation_interest: Interest in AI, automation, or data-driven solutions is a non-scoring JD signal; statements such as 'Passionate about AI' do not add JD Match Score.

inference_rules: FastAPI may support Python evidence when it is used in a development context.
Make.com is transferable to n8n, not direct evidence of n8n.
Kubernetes is adjacent to Docker, not evidence that Docker was used.
Using ChatGPT does not prove Prompt Engineering.
Using Gemini API does not automatically prove Context Engineering.
RAG or dynamic context construction may support Context Engineering.
Related technology must not automatically imply competence in another technology.

criteria.name: Academic Relevance
jd_basis: Relevant academic preparation can support the internship's AI, data, NLP, and machine-learning requirements.
criteria.description: Holistic relevance of academic background to the role; no individual education field is mandatory.
positive_evidence_examples: Degree or major in a relevant field
Relevant NLP, machine-learning, data, or AI coursework
weak_evidence_examples: Degree title with no relevant field, coursework, concentration, or training context
do_not_infer: GPA, university ranking, faculty, study year, or expected graduation as score inputs
Missing education metadata as a negative result

criteria.name: Python Programming
jd_basis: Qualification: proficiency in Python programming.
criteria.description: Ability to use Python in relevant development, data, or AI work.
positive_evidence_examples: Developed a FastAPI backend using Python
weak_evidence_examples: Python listed in a skills section with no usage context
do_not_infer: General programming experience as Python experience

criteria.name: Prompt Engineering
jd_basis: Responsibility: design, develop, and refine prompts.
Qualification: prompt engineering.
criteria.description: Designing and improving prompts to guide AI behavior reliably.
do_not_infer: LLM usage alone as Prompt Engineering

criteria.name: Context Engineering
jd_basis: Qualification: context engineering.
criteria.description: Constructing, selecting, or managing context so an AI application receives useful grounded inputs.
positive_evidence_examples: RAG implemented with explicit context selection, preparation, or assembly
Document grounding or dynamic context injection
weak_evidence_examples: Called a hosted LLM API without context design details
do_not_infer: Gemini or OpenAI API usage alone as Context Engineering
sending document text/data to an LLM
OCR followed by LLM processing
document extraction pipelines
using Gemini/OpenAI/another LLM on extracted data
generic preprocessing before an LLM
merely mentioning RAG/LLMs without showing context-handling work

criteria.name: AI System / Workflow Design
jd_basis: Responsibility: design AI application structure, workflow, and use.
criteria.description: Designing practical AI application flows, components, or integrations.
positive_evidence_examples: Mapped an AI workflow from input to output
Integrated an AI capability into a real system
do_not_infer: Using an AI product as evidence of designing an AI system

criteria.name: Analytical & Problem Solving
jd_basis: Qualification: strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
criteria.description: Analyzing problems and applying a reasoned solution in relevant work or projects.
positive_evidence_examples: Level 3: clear hands-on analytical/problem-solving evidence identifying a meaningful problem or constraint and showing an action, technical solution, optimization, or measured outcome

Level 4: explicitly exceptional analytical depth beyond normal hands-on problem solving (e.g., explicit root-cause diagnosis, systematic experimentation, comparison of multiple alternatives with explicit trade-offs)
weak_evidence_examples: Self-rating as a problem solver without an example
do_not_infer: A generic teamwork claim as analytical problem solving
Metrics, quantified outcomes, or successfully solving a difficult problem alone are not enough for Level 4
Multiple separate Level 3 examples or projects with good outcomes must not be combined to manufacture Level 4
When Level 3 versus Level 4 is ambiguous, or if strong hands-on problem solving is demonstrated without explicit deeper analytical process, choose Level 3

criteria.name: Requirement Understanding & Collaboration
jd_basis: Responsibility: work with users or the business-development team to understand system requirements.
Responsibility: collaborate closely with software engineers.
criteria.description: Working with stakeholders or teammates to clarify needs and deliver a shared solution.
positive_evidence_examples: Gathered requirements from users or stakeholders
Collaborated with engineers to deliver a feature
Translated business needs into implementation work
weak_evidence_examples: Listed team player without collaboration context
do_not_infer: Individual project work as stakeholder collaboration

criteria.name: Testing & Evaluation
jd_basis: Responsibility: test AI applications and evaluate their performance.
criteria.description: Testing behavior or assessing outcomes to improve an application.
positive_evidence_examples: Created or ran tests for an application
weak_evidence_examples: Claimed interest in quality without testing activity
do_not_infer: Deploying an application as proof it was tested

criteria.name: LLM / Generative AI
jd_basis: Responsibility: use Large Language Models to develop AI applications.
criteria.description: Understanding relevant to applying LLMs or generative AI in an application context.
positive_evidence_examples: Explained LLM behavior, limitations, or integration choices
do_not_infer: AI interest alone as LLM or Generative AI knowledge

criteria.name: Natural Language Processing
jd_basis: Qualification: foundational understanding of Natural Language Processing (NLP).
criteria.description: Foundational NLP concepts or their applied use.
positive_evidence_examples: Text classification, extraction, or language-processing project
weak_evidence_examples: Mentioned text data without NLP method or learning context
do_not_infer: Using an LLM as proof of NLP fundamentals

criteria.name: Machine Learning Fundamentals
jd_basis: Qualification: foundational understanding of machine-learning concepts.
criteria.description: Foundational machine-learning knowledge relevant to AI application work.
positive_evidence_examples: Built or evaluated a machine-learning workflow
weak_evidence_examples: Listed machine learning with no context
do_not_infer: Data analysis alone as machine-learning knowledge

criteria.name: API
jd_basis: Qualification: experience working with APIs.
criteria.description: Practical work with application programming interfaces.
positive_evidence_examples: Built or consumed a REST API
Integrated an API into an application
weak_evidence_examples: Named an API without describing use
do_not_infer: General web browsing as API experience

criteria.name: JSON / Structured Data
jd_basis: Qualification: experience working with JSON.
criteria.description: Using JSON or comparable structured data in a practical workflow.
positive_evidence_examples: Validated structured data in an application
Used JSON in an API integration

Demonstrated creation, transformation, normalization, validation, or manipulation of structured tabular data such as CSV or normalized records is direct evidence of the Structured Data portion of this criterion.
weak_evidence_examples: Mentioned data formats without use context
do_not_infer: Using an API as automatic proof of JSON handling
Do not claim explicit JSON experience unless JSON is actually supported by the resume
Do not classify demonstrated structured-data work as none merely because the format is CSV rather than JSON
Do not downgrade demonstrated structured-data work to equivalent merely because JSON itself is not mentioned

criteria.name: Automation Pipeline / Integration
jd_basis: Qualification: experience with automation pipelines.
Qualification: interest in automation and data-driven solutions.
criteria.description: Building or integrating automated workflows that move data or trigger useful actions.
positive_evidence_examples: Automated a recurring data or business process
do_not_infer: A manual multi-step process as an automation pipeline

criteria.name: n8n
jd_basis: Preferred qualification: n8n experience.
criteria.description: Preferred workflow-automation technology; it is not a mandatory requirement.
weak_evidence_examples: Read about n8n without a usage example
do_not_infer: Make.com or another automation platform as direct n8n experience

criteria.name: SQL
jd_basis: Preferred qualification: SQL experience.
criteria.description: Preferred structured-query capability; it is not a mandatory requirement.
positive_evidence_examples: Used SQL for data analysis or application features
explicit practical evidence such as writing queries, schema/table work, joins/aggregations, or CRUD/data manipulation
weak_evidence_examples: SQL or database product names (MySQL, PostgreSQL) appearing only in a skills list without explicit project/work evidence
do_not_infer: NoSQL database usage as SQL experience
Listing several related database technologies does not turn mention-only evidence into demonstrated usage

criteria.name: Docker
jd_basis: Preferred qualification: Docker experience.
criteria.description: Preferred containerization technology; it is not a mandatory requirement.
positive_evidence_examples: Containerized a FastAPI service using Docker
Wrote Dockerfiles or Docker Compose configurations
weak_evidence_examples: Recognized container concepts without Docker use
do_not_infer: Kubernetes as evidence that Docker was used

criteria.name: Cloud Platform
jd_basis: Preferred qualification: Cloud platform experience.
criteria.description: Preferred cloud-platform experience; it is not a mandatory requirement.
positive_evidence_examples: Level 2 is for application-level use or integration of a managed cloud service without explicit cloud infrastructure/deployment responsibility
weak_evidence_examples: A cloud platform or service is only mentioned in a skills/tool list, with no demonstrated use
do_not_infer: Using a hosted developer tool as cloud-platform experience
Do not infer cloud engineering responsibility merely from the service being hosted by a cloud provider or an application using a managed database/service
Do not infer cloud engineering from generic statements such as scalable architecture unless explicit cloud engineering responsibilities are also supported

If the resume clearly shows application-level use of a managed cloud service but does not explicitly show cloud deployment/infrastructure/configuration responsibility, choose Level 2 rather than Level 3
